content: If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to note that this is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. To use this medication, take it by mouth with or without food as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily. If stomach upset occurs, take it with food. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, weight, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve before completing the course. Common side effects may include diarrhea, stomach upset, changes in taste, nausea, or vomiting. This medication may also cause harmless discoloration of urine, sweat, saliva, or tears to a brown-orange color, which will resolve once the medication is stopped. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. In rare cases, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking rifabutin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other rifamycins (such as rifampin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Rifabutin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (such as the typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. If you have HIV, breastfeeding may transmit the virus to your baby. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Rifabutin can accelerate the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, which could result in pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, lab and/or medical tests (such as liver function tests and complete blood counts) should be performed regularly. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in May 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete and personalized advice regarding this medication and your health needs.
